---
title: "Import and analyse ASV portal data with R"
format:
  html:
    toc: false
---

This tutorial walks through the main steps needed to integrate ASV portal data in R and explore biodiversity patterns. As a case study, we use COI metabarcoding data from the [Insect Biome Atlas](https://www.insectbiomeatlas.org/){target="_blank"} (IBA) project to examine arthropod community composition across habitat types in Sweden.

In 2019, the IBA project collected arthropod samples at 200 sites spanning six habitat types — forest, cropland, wetland, grassland, urban and alpine. The full Swedish IBA dataset comprises four COI datasets that differ in both sampling method (Malaise trap vs. soil/litter extraction) and DNA extraction protocol (ethanol preservation, homogenate, or lysate). Here, we combine the homogenate-extracted Malaise-trap samples with a downsampled subset of the lysate-extracted Malaise-trap samples.

1. [Set up the environment](tutorial-01-setup.qmd) — Access the workshop RStudio environment (or run locally)
2. [Prepare data](tutorial-02-prep.qmd) — Load, merge and aggregate data sourced from the ASV portal
3. [Map samples](tutorial-03-map.qmd) — Filter, balance and map sampling coverage across Sweden and habitat types
4. [Community composition](tutorial-04-pcoa.qmd) — Beta diversity: Spearman dissimilarity and PCoA
5. [Within-sample diversity](tutorial-05-shannon.qmd) — Alpha diversity: Shannon index by habitat
6. [Taxonomic composition](tutorial-06-barplots.qmd) — Taxonomic barplots across habitat types

[Get started →](tutorial-01-setup.qmd)
